news.take: Two cryogenic modules cooled as one system, a step toward chaining hundreds of chips. The fault-tolerant target stays 2029.
news.title: IBM links its first modular quantum fridges

news.take: Agent-to-agent and agent-to-tool standards now share one neutral home. Google Cloud, Azure and AWS all support A2A.
news.title: A2A joins MCP under the Agentic AI Foundation

news.take: A 30B open model to tune on your own data. NVIDIA claims its router matches frontier accuracy at a third of the cost.
news.title: NVIDIA's open Nemotron 3.5 targets cheaper agent work

news.take: One stolen npm token let it republish every package a maintainer owned. More than 400 packages were hit.
news.title: Microsoft dissects the ChainDrop worm

points: Survey: 1,719 respondents in 97 nations, May to June 2026
32% skipped buying software because agents could build it in-house
39% expect AI-related job cuts next year; 14% saw them in the past year
news.take: 40% of large firms are scaling agents, yet only 37% see any profit impact. The 6% who do redesign their workflows.
news.title: McKinsey: 40% of large firms scale agents, 37% see profit

news.take: Grippers succeed on 74% to 90% of tasks. Multi-finger hands manage 32% to 92%, which DeepMind calls still challenging.
news.title: DeepMind's Gemini Robotics 2 runs whole humanoids

news.take: SBOMs should now carry the author's signature, a version and component hashes, and cover open-source, AI and SaaS software.
news.title: US agencies update the minimum elements of an SBOM

news.take: npm 12 turns install scripts off by default, and Dependabot waits three days before proposing a new version.
news.title: GitHub lists its defences against npm worms

news.take: Servers can sit behind ordinary load balancers and authorisation is tighter. Older transports get a twelve-month exit.
news.title: MCP's new specification goes stateless

news.take: A 1.5B domain-tuned model scored 0.43 F1 against 0.12 or less, and ran 23–95 times faster on CPU. Small test set.
news.title: A small medical model beats compressed general models

news.take: High-risk duties move to December 2027 and August 2028. A ban on AI-made non-consensual intimate images is added.
news.title: EU AI Omnibus moves high-risk duties to late 2027

news.take: When agents beat people at every budget, 'how long a task' stops meaning much. METR surveys cost-based replacements.
news.title: METR: the time-horizon yardstick is running out

news.take: Published in Nature. An AI agent used the chip's own error signals to cut logical errors 20% beyond expert calibration.
news.title: Google: a quantum chip that retunes itself mid-run

news.take: Mistral models come to Azure, Azure Local and fully disconnected sites, aimed at regulated and public bodies.
news.title: Microsoft and Mistral offer European models that run offline

news.take: Transparency duties apply from 2 August 2026. AI systems already on the market need machine-readable marking by 2 December.
news.title: EU sets out how to label AI-generated content

news.take: RFC 9999 lets remote-attestation results travel across CBOR, JWT and X.509 formats, a building block for verifiable trust.
news.title: IETF standardises a wrapper for attestation evidence

news.take: AI agents bought from merchants such as Frasers and lastminute.com for cardholders, within limits the shoppers set.
news.title: Visa runs live agent purchases with 31 European banks

news.take: A US directive on 12 June forced a shutdown for all users. Controls lifted on 30 June; access returned with an extra safety filter.
news.title: Anthropic restores Fable 5 after an export-control pause

news.take: High-value federal systems must move by 2030 or 2031. Contractors must meet federal security standards by the end of 2030.
news.title: US sets 2030 deadlines for post-quantum federal systems

news.take: 565 TWh in 2026, with AI servers taking 31%. Gartner says grid supply will not keep up with planned construction.
news.title: Gartner: data centres use 26% more power this year

news.take: The money funds its roadmap from today's systems to fault-tolerant machines.
news.title: IBM commits more than $10bn to quantum

news.take: By 2027, over 65% of teams using agentic coding will move control and validation to automated platforms.
news.title: Gartner: coding agents make the IDE optional

news.take: Walmart, Target, Nike and others support it. A universal cart lets shoppers check out across retailers in Search and Gemini.
news.title: Google widens its Universal Commerce Protocol for retailers

points: Public models: about 12 hours at 50% success, 1.5 hours at 80%
About 40% of surveyed staff gave agents unrestricted commands on low-stakes work
METR wants regular third-party checks of how labs use AI internally
news.take: Agents finished projects that take people days. On long tasks, 16% of the wins broke the rules, and monitoring had gaps.
news.title: METR: agents finish multi-day projects, sometimes by breaking rules

news.take: Google DeepMind's system proposed leukaemia and liver-fibrosis drug candidates that worked in cell tests.
news.title: Nature: an AI co-scientist's ideas hold up in the lab

news.take: AI is surfacing flaws in code Microsoft had already studied closely. Expect bigger releases and more out-of-band fixes.
news.title: Microsoft explains its growing Patch Tuesdays

news.take: The hosts argue faster patching alone will not hold now that many models can find zero-days. Prevention matters more.
news.title: Risky Business: you can't patch your way out

news.take: Shrink what faces the internet first, turn on automatic updates, and replace what cannot be patched.
news.title: UK NCSC: prepare for a patch wave

news.take: Start-ups raised $12.6bn in 2025, 6.3 times the year before. Quantum computing revenue passed $1bn.
news.title: McKinsey: quantum reaches a commercial tipping point

news.take: Both say identity and permissions for agents are unsolved. OpenAI's models will run on a mix of Trainium and GPUs.
news.title: Stratechery: Altman and Garman on agents inside AWS

news.take: The inference chip claims 80% better performance per dollar than the last generation.
news.title: Google's eighth-generation TPUs split training and inference

news.take: Four European groups won. Three reached SEAL-3 on the new sovereignty scale; one, using Google technology, reached SEAL-2.
news.title: Commission awards EUR 180m of sovereign cloud contracts

news.take: It warns of 'cognitive debt' as AI writes more code, and treats sandboxing and zero trust as the baseline for agents.
news.title: Thoughtworks Radar 34: put coding agents on a leash

news.take: Three-quarters of a robot's lifetime cost is setup and re-engineering. Software-defined robots could halve that.
news.title: BCG: back robot capabilities, not body shapes

news.take: It urges other engineering teams to move authentication and digital signatures first.
news.title: Google sets 2029 for its post-quantum switch

news.take: Nokia Bell Labs ran backpropagation on a photonic chip and matched a digital model at over 90% accuracy.
news.title: Nature: a light-based chip trains itself

news.take: Analyst Dylan Patel says new fabs take two to three years and memory stays tight until late 2027 or 2028.
news.title: Dwarkesh Podcast: chips and memory, not power, cap AI

news.take: An AI agent paid within preset limits using Mastercard Agent Pay. Santander now moves to wider testing, not yet a rollout.
news.title: Santander and Mastercard: Europe's first live agent payment

news.take: It covers agent security, identity and authorisation, with open protocols as one of three pillars.
news.title: NIST starts an AI agent standards initiative

news.take: $12.6bn in 2026 and $23.1bn in 2027, the year Europe overtakes North America.
news.title: Gartner: Europe's sovereign cloud spending to rise 83%

news.take: After March 2026 there are no more fixes of any kind. About half of cloud-native environments depend on it.
news.title: Kubernetes leaders: leave Ingress NGINX now

news.take: Fewer than 20 companies will run them in production. Wheeled multi-purpose robots give better uptime for the money.
news.title: Gartner: humanoid robots stay rare until 2028

points: Refunds, price and product familiarity decide whether people hand over control
Merchants risk the biggest loss of control over the customer
Partnering with card issuers and AI platforms is one way to stay visible
news.take: 81% expect to use AI when shopping and 42% would hand an agent full control for at least one category. Trust is the barrier.
news.title: BCG: four in ten shoppers would let an agent buy
